newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat extends gains late on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat extends gains late on short-covering.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures extended their gains in continued short-covering and on spillover from CBOT wheat and soybeans, traders said.
"It's feeding on itself," a trader said. "The bottom line is that this is short-covering being done on light volumes."

Traders said that with less than two weeks to go until first notice date for delivery on KCBT December wheat, individuals who were short Dec were rolling their shorts out to March, causing a widening of the December/March inversion.
"This has caused a dramatic widening of the Dec/March spread," a trader said.
Traders said the December/March spread was being bid late at 39 cents per bushel. It traded late Tuesday at 33 cents.
KCBT wheat settled unofficially 2-1/2 to 16-1/4 cents higher, with Dec up 16-1/4 cents at $4.40-3/4.
CIS was said to have sold at least two million March bushels.
